s1.syndrome_frame: painful vulvar swelling with signs of inflammation
salient_findings: extremely painful during the past week
firm mass of the left labia majora without signs of inflammation
key_facts: left labial swelling with signs of inflammation
5 × 5 cm firm swelling of the left labia majora

raw.syndrome_frame: painful vulvar swelling with signs of inflammation
salient_findings: extremely painful during the past week
firm mass of the left labia majora without signs of inflammation
key_facts: left labial swelling with signs of inflammation
5 × 5 cm firm swelling of the left labia majora

shortlist.label: Bartholin's abscess
shortlist.why_kept: initial clinical diagnosis with signs of inflammation and response to parenteral antibiotics

shortlist.label: Vulvar fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: firm swelling of the left labia majora without signs of inflammation, consistent with a benign tumor

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of a firm, non-cystic swelling in the vulvar region

shortlist.label: Vulvar cancer
shortlist.why_kept: although less likely, cannot be ruled out without further investigation due to the patient's age and symptoms

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: rare but possible cause of a firm, painless swelling in the vulvar region

raw.rationale: The firm, 5 × 5 cm swelling of the left labia majora without signs of inflammation, and the patient's response to initial antibiotic treatment which may have been coincidental, suggests a benign tumor such as vulvar fibroma, which is more likely given the absence of systemic symptoms and the description of the mass.

rejected.label: Bartholin's abscess
rejected.why: Initial diagnosis was reconsidered due to the swelling being firm and not cystic after inflammation subsided

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: The description of the mass as firm and 5 × 5 cm is less typical for an epidermoid cyst, which is usually smaller and more cystic

rejected.label: Vulvar cancer
rejected.why: The patient's age and the description of the mass are not typical for vulvar cancer, which is more common in older women and often presents with more sinister symptoms

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: This rare tumor can present as a large, firm mass but is less likely given the patient's age and the lack of other characteristic features such as a history of growth over time or local recurrence after attempted removal
